title: Coworkers Divide Credit for a Project Neither Fully Owns
script: Tara: [firm] The client keeps thanking you exclusively for the proposal, Deni, and I've said nothing at all for three meetings running now.
Deni: [surprised] I hadn't actually noticed the pattern, honestly, though I believe you noticed it considerably earlier than I did myself.
Tara: [measured] I'm not accusing you of engineering it deliberately. I think it's simply easier for clients to credit whoever spoke last in the room.
Deni: [thoughtful] Which happened to be me, repeatedly, mostly because you were the one actually building the analysis while I presented it afterward.
Tara: [honest] I don't need a grand public correction, for what it's worth. I need you to notice, and mention my name occasionally without my having to request it.
Deni: [gently] That's a fair, considerably more modest request than I'd braced myself for when you asked to talk privately this morning.
Tara: [wry] Adab doesn't obligate me to suffer silently, whatever version of humility some people apparently mistake it for around here.
Deni: [conceding] No, it doesn't, and I should have been distributing credit accurately without needing the correction at all from you.
Tara: [curious] What happens at tomorrow's meeting, practically speaking, now that we've actually named this out loud between us.
Deni: [determined] I open by crediting the analysis explicitly, by name, before I present a single slide of it to anyone.
Tara: [warmly] That's more than I was strictly asking for, though I won't pretend I'm not pleased to hear it from you.
Deni: [honest] You should have asked sooner, frankly. I'd rather correct this quickly than have you privately cataloguing three more meetings of silence.
Tara: [reflective] I think I stayed quiet hoping you'd notice unprompted, which was probably unfair to both of us in its own particular way.
Deni: [warmly] Probably, yes, though I'd rather you'd said something in meeting one than carried it politely for three meetings straight.
Tara: [smiling] Noted, for next time. Though I'm hoping there won't actually need to be a next time, honestly.

quiz.question: What has Tara noticed happening over three meetings?
options: Deni has been criticizing her work
The client keeps thanking Deni exclusively for the proposal while she has said nothing
Deni has stopped attending meetings
The client wants to end the contract
quiz.explanation: Tara notices the client keeps thanking Deni exclusively for the proposal, and she's said nothing for three meetings.

quiz.question: Why does Deni suggest the client credits him rather than Tara?
options: Because he did all the actual work
Because it's easier for clients to credit whoever spoke last in the room, which was him
Because Tara asked him to take credit
Because the client dislikes Tara
quiz.explanation: Tara suggests it's simply easier for clients to credit whoever spoke last, which happened to be Deni.

quiz.question: What does Tara say she actually needs, rather than a grand public correction?
options: A formal apology in writing
For Deni to notice and mention her name occasionally without her having to request it
A raise in salary
To be removed from the project
quiz.explanation: Tara says she needs Deni to notice and mention her name occasionally without her having to ask.

quiz.question: What does Tara say about adab and suffering silently?
options: Adab requires suffering silently as true humility
Adab doesn't obligate her to suffer silently, despite some people's mistaken view of humility
Adab has nothing to do with workplace credit
Adab only applies to family situations
quiz.explanation: Tara states adab doesn't obligate her to suffer silently, which some people apparently mistake for humility.

quiz.question: What does Deni commit to doing at tomorrow's meeting?
options: Avoiding the client's questions
Crediting the analysis explicitly, by name, before presenting a single slide
Asking Tara to present instead of him
Ending the project early
quiz.explanation: Deni commits to opening the meeting by explicitly crediting the analysis by name before presenting anything.
